## What The Business Is

Cisco Systems is a large enterprise technology vendor centered on networking infrastructure, with adjacent security, observability, collaboration, cloud-management, compute, and services offerings. It sells hardware, software, subscriptions, and support to enterprises, public-sector customers, telecom/service providers, cloud providers, and partners; since the Splunk acquisition, its story is increasingly framed around secure networking plus data/observability for AI-era operations. ([cisco.com](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/about/index.html))

## What It Does

Cisco’s core products connect and secure digital infrastructure: campus and data-center switching, routing, wireless, optical networking via Acacia, Silicon One-based systems, industrial IoT, firewalls/SASE/XDR, collaboration devices/Webex, and Splunk-led observability/security analytics. In the May 13, 2026 quarter, product revenue was $12.1B and services revenue was $3.7B; Networking revenue grew 25% year over year, Observability grew 3%, Collaboration declined 1%, and Security was flat. ([newsroom.cisco.com](https://newsroom.cisco.com/c/r/newsroom/en/us/a/y2026/m05/cisco-reports-third-quarter-earnings.html?source=rss))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Cisco’s Q3 FY2026 results, reported May 13 for the quarter ended April 25, showed record revenue of $15.8B, up 12% year over year, with GAAP EPS up 37% and non-GAAP EPS up 10%; total product orders rose 35%, or 19% excluding hyperscalers. Management also lifted FY2026 guidance to $62.8B–$63.0B of revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $4.27–$4.29. ([newsroom.cisco.com](https://newsroom.cisco.com/c/r/newsroom/en/us/a/y2026/m05/cisco-reports-third-quarter-earnings.html?source=rss))

AI infrastructure demand was the clearest upside theme in the transcript and release: Cisco said hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders reached $5.3B year-to-date and raised expected FY2026 AI infrastructure orders to $9B, while raising expected FY2026 AI infrastructure revenue to $4B. Campus networking orders grew more than 25%, and data-center switching orders grew more than 40%, supporting management’s claim that enterprise AI and campus refresh are driving a multi-year demand cycle. ([newsroom.cisco.com](https://newsroom.cisco.com/c/r/newsroom/en/us/a/y2026/m05/cisco-reports-third-quarter-earnings.html?source=rss))

Cisco continued adding product and M&A pieces around AI security and observability. It announced intent to acquire Galileo on April 9, 2026 for AI observability/trust tooling, and Astrix Security on May 4, 2026 for securing non-human identities such as API keys, service accounts, OAuth tokens, and AI agents. ([cisco.com](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/about/corporate-strategy-office/acquisitions/acquisitions-list-names.html))

At Cisco Live U.S. in June, Cisco emphasized AI-ready data centers, resilient infrastructure, future workplaces, Cisco Cloud Control, Cisco Live Protect, Cisco IQ, agentic security, and next-generation Silicon One capabilities, positioning these as a unified platform response to AI-driven operational complexity. ([newsroom.cisco.com](https://newsroom.cisco.com/c/r/newsroom/en/us/a/y2026/m06/cisco-live-u-s-leading-in-the-agentic-ai-age.html))

Cisco also announced the Universal Quantum Switch on April 23, a working research prototype designed to route and preserve quantum information over standard telecom fiber at room temperature; this is early-stage, but it reinforces Cisco’s long-horizon networking R&D narrative. ([newsroom.cisco.com](https://newsroom.cisco.com/c/r/newsroom/en/us/a/y2026/m04/cisco-introduces-universal-quantum-switch-advancing-the-path-to-a-quantum-network.html))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Margins and mix

## Transcript Read — Long Case

- AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers now expected ~$9B in FY26, up from prior $5B target, with FY27 revenue guide of at least $6B
- Total product orders grew 35% y/y; ex-hyperscaler orders up 19%, accelerating from 10% prior quarter
- Enterprise data center switching orders up >40% y/y, campus switching >25%, wireless >40% with WiFi 7 penetration accelerating
- Acacia optics had $1B+ orders in Q3, on track for >200% growth in FY26; strong design wins including first Silicon One P200 scale-across wins
- Gross margin stabilized at 66% despite memory cost headwinds; operating margin guided 34-35% with bottom line growing faster than top line
- Restructuring to reallocate resources to silicon, optics, security, AI signals confidence in growth areas
- Supply chain advantage from in-house silicon design and advanced purchase commitments ($6.7B increase in 90 days)

Rationale: AI infrastructure orders exceeded expectations by a wide margin, with FY26 order target raised from $5B to $9B and FY27 AI revenue visibility of at least $6B. Enterprise demand broad-based and accelerating, driven by AI/security modernization tailwinds. Competitive moat in Silicon One and optics driving hyperscaler wins. Margin headwinds mitigated by price increases and supply chain control, with operating leverage improving.

## Transcript Read — Short Case

- Possible modest pull-forward of orders due to price increase announcements, though management believes impact was limited
- Gross margin still down 260bps y/y, with mix shift to hardware a headwind; memory costs remain elevated
- AI revenue recognition lags orders significantly ($4B revenue on $9B orders FY26), indicating long lead times and lumpy execution

## Bull Case
- AI infrastructure orders inflected hard: FY26 order target raised from $5B to $9B, with FY27 AI revenue visibility of at least $6B. This is genuine new TAM, not just share shift.
- Enterprise demand is broad and accelerating: ex-hyperscaler orders +19% (vs +10% prior quarter), campus switching +25%, data-center switching +40%, Acacia optics on track for >200% growth — a multi-year refresh cycle layered on the AI cycle.
- FCF is optically depressed: TTM FCF of $11.8B is below both FY24 and FY25 despite revenue growth ~12%, due to a $6.7B increase in advance purchase commitments and inventory build. As those normalize and AI orders convert to revenue, FCF should snap back well above trend, mechanically deflating today's elevated multiple.
- Margin defense is credible: gross margin stabilized at 66% despite memory costs; operating margin guided 34–35%; EPS growing faster than revenue.

## Bear Case
- The stock has already re-rated massively: market cap of $441B vs a 3-year mean of ~$253B (+75%). The AI order inflection is largely in the price.
- Current EV/FCF of ~39x is roughly 2.5x Cisco's historical norm and well above the 3-year average FCF/EV yield (5.4% vs 2.5% now). This is a valuation built for a hypergrowth story on a company guiding non-AI growth back to 4–6% in FY27.
- Hyperscaler revenue is low-margin, lumpy hardware; mix shift already drove gross margin down 260bps y/y. AI revenue recognition lags orders badly ($4B revenue on $9B orders).
- Possible order pull-forward ahead of price increases, tariff/memory cost risk, and a persistent Splunk cloud-transition drag on Security (flat y/y).

## Multiple Re-Rating
- **Current implied multiple:** 464,833 / 11,788 = **~39.4x EV/FCF**
- **12-month forward multiple:** **~30x**
- **Direction:** **CONTRACT**
- **Drivers:**
  1. **FCF normalization deflates the optical multiple.** Today's 39x reflects working-capital/purchase-commitment-depressed FCF. As FCF recovers toward $14–15B, the market doesn't need to pay 39x to keep the stock at these levels — the multiple mechanically compresses even in a flat-to-modestly-lower price scenario.
  2. **AI catalyst substantially priced.** The move from a $5B to $9B AI order target is public and reflected in a market cap 75% above the 3-year mean. FY27 guidance already flags non-AI deceleration to 4–6%; the second derivative of growth turns negative outside the hyperscaler bucket.
  3. **Mix and quality of incremental growth.** Hyperscaler hardware carries lower gross margins and lumpy recognition — the market historically pays less, not more, for that revenue than for Cisco's subscription/software base. A maturing franchise re-accelerating on hardware doesn't sustain a near-40x cash-flow multiple.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF:** Revenue tracking to ~$63B FY26 and growing high-single digits into FY27 (~$66–67B run-rate). FCF was suppressed this year by supply-chain pre-buys and inventory build; assuming partial normalization plus AI revenue conversion, I forecast forward TTM FCF of **~$14,500M** (a ~23% recovery, still only ~22% FCF margin, below FY24 levels relative to revenue).
- **Applied multiple:** **30x EV/FCF** (contracted from 39.4x per above) — still a substantial premium to Cisco's historical ~15–18x, crediting the AI order book and Silicon One/optics moat, but acknowledging the catalyst is largely priced.
- **Forward EV:** 14,500 × 30 = **$435,000M**
- **EV → Market cap bridge:** Current gap = EV − MC = 464,833 − 440,613 = **$24,220M net debt**. Holding the gap constant:
- **Forward market cap:** 435,000 − 24,220 = **~$410,780M** (~7% below today's $440.6B — modest downside as multiple compression slightly outpaces FCF recovery).
